source.version: NBER Working Paper 33641, April 2025; The Cybernetic Teammate: A Field Experiment on Generative AI Reshaping Teamwork and Expertise (PDF pp. 1-2). The saved working paper is not the later Organization Science article in the citation record.
source.supplement_used: Appendices A-C and Figure A1 in the same PDF, PDF pp. 47-54. No separate supplement was found among this paper's files.

studies.label: P&G product-development field experiment: individual or cross-functional team, with or without generative AI
studies.cluster_se_treatment: Individuals were assigned within business-unit/geography strata and paired in team conditions (PDF pp. 9-10). Strata and formed production teams are not pre-existing randomized clusters. Regressions use one row per solution and heteroskedasticity-robust SEs (PDF p. 12); no participant clustering or random effects are stated.

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 9, Section 3.2 (analysis total); PDF p. 41, Table 1, Individuals and Team participants rows (columns No AI, + AI). The total and arm counts conflict.
counts_source.quote:
Our analyses focus on 776 of these participants who were randomly assigned across four conditions.
Individuals
154
155
Team participants
230 (115 Teams)
252 (126 Teams)

arms.name: Individual No AI (Control)
arms.description: Works alone without AI on the initial scored task; AI training follows afterward.

arms.name: Team No AI (T1)
arms.description: Randomly paired Commercial and R&D professionals work jointly without AI and submit a shared solution. Table 1 reports 115 teams.

arms.name: Individual + AI (T2)
arms.description: Works alone with the GPT-4-based tool after one-hour training and recommended prompts.

arms.name: Team + AI (T3)
arms.description: Randomly paired Commercial and R&D professionals use the tool after the same training and submit a shared solution. Table 1 reports 126 teams.

studies.country: Countries not stated; Europe and Americas
studies.task: Develop a new product, packaging, communication, or retail-execution solution to a real innovation problem in the employee's own business unit.

ai_tool.name: GenAI tool built on GPT-4 and accessed through Microsoft Azure; the July workshop used GPT-4o
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 10, Section 3.2 and footnote 10; Appendix C, PDF pp. 50-53. Model release years are not stated; workshop dates on PDF p. 8 are study dates.

preregistration.where: AEA RCT Registry, AEARCTR-0013603; https://www.socialscienceregistry.org/trials/13603 (PDF p. 2 and p. 8, footnote 3). The saved PDF says the plan is embargoed.

estimates.notes: Model 1. n_units is the printed observation count for the entire multi-arm regression, not this two-arm comparison. n_total is null because a two-arm people total is not printed. estimates.outcome: Bimodality of the distribution of solution technicality
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Condition-level bimodality coefficient of expert-rated technical versus commercial orientation. Each solution is rated on a 1-7 Likert scale; the retained statistic describes the distribution over team outputs.

sources.locator: PDF p. 18, Section 6.3; Figure 11 on PDF p. 39
sources.quote: Without AI, teams exhibit a clear bimodal distribution (bimodality coefficient = 0.564)

sources.locator: PDF p. 48, Appendix B.3
sources.quote: Additionally, evaluators assessed the technical versus commercial orientation of each solution on a separate 1-7 Likert scale.

estimates.notes: The treatment_mean/control_mean slots hold printed arm-level bimodality coefficients for this set-level outcome, not average technicality ratings. Higher means greater bimodality, not necessarily greater creativity or diversity. The paper describes similar overall technical content and reduced bimodality with AI. No SE, SD, test, interval, or analysis-specific count is reported. Nothing was digitized from the density plot.

open_items: The narrative analysis count conflicts with Table 1 arm counts. n_analyzed transcribes the printed narrative count, not the screening form's calculated total. Which participants enter the tables, and whether any non-randomized people are included, remains unclear.

Initial counts at random assignment and the number reassigned from incomplete teams are not stated (PDF p. 10, footnote 8). The narrative analysis count is not an unambiguous pre-attrition randomization count, so n_randomized is null.

Direct coefficients and SEs for printed pairwise tests are absent. Other full-sample active-comparison and AI-design contrasts are qualitative only. No differences were calculated from baseline-relative coefficients.

Raw quality arm means and participant-level SDs, and SDs for length and the top-decile indicator, are absent. Appendix B.4 evaluation variance components are not arm-specific participant SDs and were not converted.
Control Mean values vary by adjustment. They are preserved as labeled, with notes that adjusted entries are model-specific reference values/intercepts rather than unconditional group means.
Semantic diversity has no printed arm levels or uncertainty; Figure 13 does not specify the embedding model or an unambiguous distance computation.
No numeric results are saved for novelty, feasibility, impact, business potential, or the claimed AI-evaluator robustness analysis.
Preregistration is stated, but the preregistered primary outcome cannot be verified from the available document. The paper explicitly names overall quality as primary.

Team arms produce shared outputs under individual assignment. Robust solution-level uncertainty is conservatively marked output for team-involving records; the codebook does not explicitly resolve this partially nested production design.

The descriptive technicality record uses treatment_mean/control_mean to preserve arm-level bimodality coefficients, not average technicality ratings. It is construct other, higher_is other, with no uncertainty or analysis-specific sample counts.
The paper names GPT-4 and GPT-4o but not their release years; ai_tool.year is null rather than the study year.
The citation record identifies a later journal version; all statistics in this extraction come from the saved NBER working paper.
notes: Extraction B. The full markdown, references and appendices included, was read in contiguous chunks; tables, figures and cited pages were checked against pymupdf PDF text. PDF indices plus one match printed page numbers wherever printed. Eligible statistic inventory: Table 2 reports baseline-relative quality coefficients and robust SEs, Control Mean entries and SEs, significance bounds, observation counts and direct team-AI-versus-team-no-AI p-values. Table 3 reports baseline-relative length coefficients and SEs, Control Mean entries, significance bounds and observation counts. Table 10 reports baseline-relative top-decile coefficients and SEs, Control Mean entries, significant team-AI bounds, observation counts and direct team-AI-versus-team-no-AI and team-AI-versus-individual-AI p-values. Section 6.3 reports the team-arm technicality bimodality coefficients. The figures do not label additional numeric arm levels or uncertainties. Rounded narrative repetitions are not separate estimates. Reliability and regression fit summaries are not treatment contrasts. All regression specifications are retained, including baseline-relative Team + AI effects omitted from parts of the screening contrast map. Primary-record recommendation under codebook section 8: s1_quality_individual_ai_vs_individual_no_ai_m1. Quality is paper-primary, individual open-chat use is closest to general chatbot assistance, and the results text and Figure 2 follow the unadjusted model. This is not verified preregistered-primary status. No totals, differences, standardized effects, SDs, SEs, intervals or figure values were calculated. No overlapping participant sample is identified in the screening record.
